newsitem.title: USA: Ill. governor welcomes movement on prison bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ill. governor welcomes movement on prison bonds.

text.p: Illinois House Democratic Leader Michael Madigan's decision to support some debt issuance for prison construction is a step in the right direction, said Mike Lawrence, spokesman for Gov. Jim Edgar.
Lawrence said Friday no decision has been made yet on proposing new general obligation bond authorization for prisons during the legislative veto session in November.

Lack of Democratic lawmaker support for previous bond authorization proposals by Edgar succeeded in derailing the governor's plan because a three-fifths majority vote of both the Republican-dominated House and Senate is needed for passage.
During the spring session of the General Assembly, Edgar had proposed nearly $218 million of prison bonding, according to a spokeswoman for the Illinois Bureau of the Budget.
A spokesman for Madigan has said he changed his mind after talking with prison workers and hoped the addition of prisons would allow the state's corrections department to deal with problems.
